name: Priestley space
description: Compact Hausdorff space where for each pair of points x,y where x is not below y, there is a clopen upset U where x is in U and y is not in U.

name: Esakia space
description: Compact Hausdorff Priestley space in which the downset of every clopen set is clopen.

name: At most countable
description: The underlying set is finite or countably infinite. This concerns the whole construction, including its limit points, rather than the finite diagram window.

name: Finite
description: The underlying set has finitely many points. Finite windows used to draw an infinite construction do not make this property true.

name: Rooted
description: The order has a least element: a point below every point of the space or frame.

name: Noetherian
description: The order has no infinite strictly ascending chain. A nonisolated least point may have transfinite depth without violating this condition.

name: Finite width
description: There is a finite uniform bound on the cardinalities of antichains in the order. For a space or poset, it is assumed only locally: for each rooted upset.

name: Greatest element
description: The order has a greatest element: a point above every point of the space or frame.

name: Isolated root
description: The order has a least element and that point is isolated in the topology.

name: Discrete
description: The topology is discrete (for posets with no specified topology, this is assumed).

name: bi-Esakia space
description: Both the space and its order-dual are Esakia spaces.

name: Finite depth
description: There is a uniform bound on the cardinality of the chains in the order.

name: Clopen maximum
description: The maximum of the space is a clopen set.

name: KM space
description: For every clopen subset, the maximum of the clopen is again clopen.

name: Extremally order-disconnected
description: The upset of the closure of a union of clopen upsets is again a clopen upset.

name: Extremally disconnected
description: Closure of a union of opens is open.

name: Finite incomparability degree
description: For every point in the order, there are finitely many points which are incomparable to it.
